question: Is there salvation outside the church?

answers.label: No: there is no salvation outside the Church
Not for those who refuse it; God can save those not at fault

overview.text: Origen had already put it as Rahab's house: outside this house, that is, outside the Church, no one is saved. Cyprian, in the 250s, coined the rule: "there is no salvation outside the Church"; one cannot have God as Father without the Church as mother. Augustine accepted it, and the Council of Florence in 1442 gave it its hardest conciliar form.
Both Catholics and Protestants kept it (Westminster: "no ordinary possibility of salvation"), while modern Catholic teaching excepts those who through no fault of their own do not know the Church.

quotes.author: Origen of Alexandria
quotes.english: Let no one, then, persuade himself, let no one deceive himself: outside this house, that is, outside the Church, no one is saved. If anyone goes outside, he becomes guilty of his own death.
quotes.original: Nemo ergo sibi persuadeat, nemo semet ipsum decipiat: extra hanc domum, id est extra ecclesiam, nemo salvatur; si quis foras exierit, mortis suae ipse fit reus.
quotes.context: On Rahab's house in Jericho (Joshua 2): everyone in the house, marked with the scarlet cord, is saved when the city falls. Origen reads the house as the Church and the cord as the sign of Christ's blood, in the sentences just before this one. The homilies survive in Rufinus's Latin; the text is Baehrens's edition (GCS 30, 1921), read from the raw scan text in the library's Joshua book, whose locked sections still hold working summaries, so this passage still wants a locked library section.

source.edition: Baehrens, GCS 30 (1921), Homilies on Joshua 3.5 (Rufinus's Latin)

quotes.author: Cyprian of Carthage
quotes.work: On the Unity of the Church
quotes.english: He cannot have God for his Father who does not have the Church for his mother. If anyone could escape who was outside Noah's ark, then he too escapes who is outside the Church.
quotes.original: habere non potest Deum patrem qui ecclesiam non habet matrem. si potuit euadere quisque extra arcam Noe fuit, et qui extra ecclesiam foris fuerit euadit.
quotes.context: Written against schism at Carthage and Rome.

quotes.author: Cyprian of Carthage
quotes.english: ... because there is no salvation outside the Church.
quotes.original: quia salus extra ecclesiam non est
quotes.context: The phrase in its first known use, about baptism by heretics.

quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo
quotes.english: There is no salvation outside the Church. Who denies it? And so whatever belongs to the Church has no value for salvation outside the Church. But it is one thing not to have, another not to have to profit.
quotes.original: salus extra ecclesiam non est. quis negat? et ideo quaecumque ipsius ecclesiae habentur, extra ecclesiam non ualent ad salutem. sed aliud est non habere, aliud non utiliter habere.
quotes.context: Augustine accepts the rule, and adds that the Church's sacraments can exist outside it without saving.

quotes.author: Council of Florence
quotes.english: It firmly believes, professes and preaches that no one outside the Catholic Church, not only pagans but also Jews and heretics and schismatics, can share in eternal life, but will go into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels, unless before the end of life they are joined to her. ... No one, however great his almsgiving, even if he sheds his blood for Christ's name, can be saved unless he stays in the bosom and unity of the Catholic Church.
quotes.original: Firmiter credit, profitetur et praedicat, nullos extra catholicam Ecclesiam exsistentes, non solum paganos, sed nec Iudaeos aut haereticos atque schismaticos, aeternae vitae fieri posse participes; sed in ignem aeternum ituros, qui paratus est diabolo et angelis eius, nisi ante finem vitae eidem fuerint aggregati ... Neminemque, quantascunque eleemosynas fecerit, etsi pro Christi nomine sanguinem effuderit, posse salvari, nisi in catholicae Ecclesiae gremio et unitate permanserit.
quotes.context: The bull Cantate Domino (4 February 1442), the decree for the Jacobites (the Coptic Christians of Egypt) at the Council of Florence, as printed in Denzinger's Enchiridion (11th edition, 1911), no. 714. It restates, in its strictest conciliar form, the rule Origen pictured and Cyprian coined, drawing on Fulgentius of Ruspe.

quotes.author: Westminster Assembly
quotes.english: The visible church, which is also catholic or universal under the gospel (not confined to one nation, as before under the law), consists of all those throughout the world that profess the true religion; and of their children: and is the kingdom of the Lord Jesus Christ, the house and family of God, out of which there is no ordinary possibility of salvation.
quotes.original: The visible church, which is also catholic or universal under the gospel (not confined to one nation, as before under the law), consists of all those throughout the world that profess the true religion; and of their children: and is the kingdom of the Lord Jesus Christ, the house and family of God, out of which there is no ordinary possibility of salvation.
quotes.context: Protestants too kept the rule, applied to the visible church of all who profess the true faith.

quotes.author: Pius IX
quotes.english: It must be held by faith that outside the Apostolic Roman Church no one can be saved ... But it must likewise be held as certain that those who labor in ignorance of the true religion, if that ignorance is invincible, are not bound by any guilt in this matter before the eyes of the Lord.
quotes.original: Tenendum quippe ex fide est, extra Apostolicam Romanam Ecclesiam salvum fieri neminem posse ... sed tamen pro certo pariter habendum est, qui verae religionis ignorantia laborent, si ea sit invincibilis, nulla ipsos obstringi huiusce rei culpa ante oculos Domini.
quotes.context: The modern Catholic reading keeps the rule and excepts those not at fault.

quotes.author: Second Vatican Council
quotes.english: Those also can attain to salvation who through no fault of their own do not know the Gospel of Christ or His Church, yet sincerely seek God and moved by grace strive by their deeds to do His will as it is known to them through the dictates of conscience.
quotes.original: Those also can attain to salvation who through no fault of their own do not know the Gospel of Christ or His Church, yet sincerely seek God and moved by grace strive by their deeds to do His will as it is known to them through the dictates of conscience.
quotes.context: Section 14 of the same document says those who know the Church is necessary and refuse to enter it cannot be saved.
